messages:
IncidentBot: INCIDENT — Elevated 429s detected on /v1/generate (hosted). Alert rule: 429_rate_pct > 5% for 5m. root_ts=1761004829
Maya L.: seeing the alert now. 429s spiking from canary region 1, looks correlated to the 08:52 canary rollout.
Maya L.: paging on-call (Dan K.) — @Dan K. are you able to take?
Dan K.: on-call, looking. pulling traces + recent deploys. ping metrics and logs.
Dan K.: DeployBot, show recent deploys for inference-service in prod last hour
DeployBot: 08:52:14 UTC — deploy=canary/rate-cap-v2 -> 10% traffic (actor: Avery S.)
Avery S.: that canary was supposed to just add smarter throttling and exemptions for system keys. didn't expect widespread 429s.
Jess R.: customer reports coming in, CS flagged ~5 customers getting continuous 429s. sample ticket — "all generation requests hit 429 within 2s"
CustomerSuccess Ben: affected customers: AcmeAnalytics, BrightLayer, Helix AI, two others. I've opened priority tickets and informed their SREs.
Dan K.: quick triage: graphs show token consumption counters dropping to zero for many accounts immediately after rollout. looks like exemption table not applied, plus token accounting delta shows double-charges for some requests.
Maya L.: high customer impact -> recommend kill-switch for rate-cap-v2. can we toggle the feature flag off for hosted?
Dan K.: executing: /flags toggle rate-cap-v2 false --env=prod --scope=hosted --actor=DanK
DeployBot: Feature flag "rate-cap-v2" set to false (actor: Dan K., time: 08:59:07 UTC)
Avery S.: confirming — I see the flag change. good catch.
Emma T.: note: Dedicated & Private deployments are NOT affected; this was a hosted-only config propagation bug.
Dan K.: while flipping flag, I noticed the exemption loader threw errors: \n```
ERROR: exemption-loader failed to merge exemptions for region=us-east-1: invalid-format at row 0
WARN: fallback to default exemptions -> none applied
```
Dan K.: also found token-accounting log showing doubled charge: \n```
INFO token-charge user=acct_zz tokens=3.0 -> charged=6.0 reason=legacy-unit-mismatch
ERROR quota-state user=acct_zz remaining=-3.0 throttled=true
```
Jess R.: so two separate bugs: exemptions didn't load, and token accounting doubled charges. both would amplify throttling.
Maya L.: status check: customers still seeing 429s?
CustomerSuccess Ben: degradation window shortened — some customers report recovery after ~2m; others still getting 429s.
Dan K.: metrics: 429 rate peaked at 22% at 08:58, dropped to 2% at 09:05 after flag flip.
IncidentBot: Annotated timeline: detection 08:56 UTC, canary deploy 08:52, flag flip 08:59, customers recovered baseline ~09:05.
Rick M.: good mitigation. need rollback of the canary to ensure config doesn't re-propagate on next rollout. who's owning rollback?
Avery S.: I'll perform a rollback of the canary orchestration to the previous config and pin it. command: \n```
kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-service-canary -n prod --to-revision=23
```
Avery S.: running rollback now.
DeployBot: Rollback triggered (deployment=inference-service-canary, to_revision=23, actor=Avery S., time=09:12:03 UTC)
Avery S.: rollback confirmed. canary serving config restored to revision 23.
Dan K.: post-rollback check: exemption loader now working against v23 config. sampled logs show exemptions merged successfully.
Dan K.: still want to root cause token accounting double-charge — suspect unit conversion change in middleware (microtokens -> tokens) from the canary.
Maya L.: escalation: assign a follow-up to eng-runtime and eng-ml to audit token accounting changes.
Rick M.: I'll take ownership of postmortem and liaise with CS. linking to incident board: https://internal/incidents/1761004829
Jess R.: customer impact note for tickets: window ~08:52–09:05 UTC, approx 5 customers affected, error 429, some requests double-counted tokens causing quota drop. advising crediting impacted customers.
CustomerSuccess Ben: requesting credits for 4 enterprise accounts; sending proposed credit amounts to finance.
Dan K.: temporary mitigation checklist captured: \n- feature flag flip (done)\n- canary rollback (done)\n- monitor 429 rate until stable (ongoing)\n- open PR to revert token-accounting change (in review)
Maya L.: on-call handoff: handing to Rick M. for postmortem and customer comms. Dan, stay on for follow-up of accounting bug.
Rick M.: ack, taking postmortem. assigning timeline items and owners.
Emma T.: logging note: add audit entry for flag change and rollback for compliance.
IncidentBot: Paging summary posted to #incidents and #eng-runtime. Severity: Sev2 -> customer-impacting with partial degradation; start_time=1761004829 end_time=1761007900 (approx).
Dan K.: preliminary root cause: canary deploy introduced two regressions — malformed exemptions config loader + token accounting unit conversion bug -> combined cause of over-throttling.
Avery S.: next steps from infra: add validation for exemptions schema in deploy pipeline, add unit tests for token accounting conversion, and require canary to run synthetic tests hitting exemptions path.
Rick M.: I'll schedule postmortem doc and follow-up meeting. owners: Rick (postmortem), Dan (fix accounting), Avery (deploy validation), Maya (customer comms), Ben (credits).
Maya L.: thanks everyone. monitoring shows 429s back to baseline for >20m. closing incident channel, will reopen if regression recurs. :white_check_mark:
Rick M.: draft incident summary to follow in #incidents. final action: retro + deploy pipeline changes within 1 week.
Jess R.: adding link to affected tickets in the postmortem when ready.
Dan K.: leaving a note for on-call rotation: if you see a sudden 429 spike after deploy, consider exemptions table + token accounting as first suspects.
IncidentBot: Thread closed by Rick M. at 09:47 UTC (last_update=1761008429)
